speaker: alice
text: First up, Europe's just smashed a massive milestone that's got renewable energy fans absolutely chuffing. <cite index='19-1,19-2'>Solar power generated more electricity than fossil fuels across the EU for the first time ever, supplying 18% of the EU's electricity</cite>. That's history in the making, folks.

speaker: charlie
text: Fair dinkum, that's massive! And speaking of tackling nasties, <cite index='11-7,11-8,11-9'>France has officially implemented a ban on products containing PFAS - those 'forever chemicals' - due to their extreme persistence in the environment. The law prohibits the sale, production, or import of PFAS-containing products where safer alternatives already exist, including cosmetics, clothing, and ski wax</cite>.

speaker: alice
text: Love it when governments actually get stuff done for the planet. And here's one that'll blow your mind - <cite index='11-3,11-5'>Dr. Toby Kiers has been awarded the 2026 Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement for her work on mycorrhizal fungi, which are responsible for drawing down around 13 billion tons of CO₂ each year - that's roughly a third of global fossil fuel emissions</cite>. Underground heroes, literally!
